proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is closer to 2–3 weeks, forecasts may peak too early and under-represent the rise/decline timing.
proposals.rationale: Primary family (SEIRS) with short reporting/admission lag; tests whether a 1-week alignment better matches timing than the current 2-week best while keeping dynamics parsimonious.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If lag varies within-season or differs across splits, fixed 2-week delay can cause systematic phase error (early/late peaks).
proposals.rationale: Carry-forward of previous best spec; serves as the anchor template for comparison while maintaining reinfection/waning-immunity behavior and a plausible hospitalization lag proxy.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If lag is shorter, forecasts may peak too late and smear rapid changes, degrading short-horizon accuracy.
proposals.rationale: Explores the upper end of the requested small delay neighborhood to capture potentially longer admission/reporting lag in this age band without adding compartments.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May be unstable across rolling splits (over-flexible), producing inconsistent peak width or tail behavior despite similar fit.
proposals.rationale: Fractional SEIRS variant to allow slightly more flexible rise/decay shapes while keeping the same short-lag observation; included sparingly given prior split-variability concerns.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can over-adjust curvature and yield sensitive parameterizations, leading to variable timing/level forecasts across splits.
proposals.rationale: Fractional counterpart to the anchor (2-week delay) to test whether fractional dynamics improve shape capture at high rate scale without changing observation semantics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If hospitalization is meaningfully lagged, this will show systematic phase mismatch (peaks too early) and poorer timing calibration.
proposals.rationale: Control template to verify whether an explicit delay is truly necessary; keeps SEIRS dynamics but maps hospitalizations directly to the infectious proxy.
